title: Your body is glowing right now

lines.text: Your body is glowing, right now. You just can't see it.
In 2009, Japanese researchers filmed people in total darkness with ultra-sensitive cameras.
They caught real visible light coming off human skin.
It's about a thousand times too weak for your eyes to detect.
It's a side effect of your metabolism. Reactive molecules from cell respiration release tiny flashes of light.
The face glowed the most, especially the cheeks, forehead and neck.
And the glow follows your body clock. Weakest late at night, brightest in the late afternoon.
So in a sense, every human being is very, very faintly bioluminescent.

sources.claim: Kobayashi et al. (PLoS ONE, 2009): the human body emits visible light about 1,000 times weaker than the eye can detect, with a daily rhythm linked to metabolism
Forehead, neck and cheeks glowed most; peak in late afternoon, weakest late at night; caused by free radicals from cell respiration
